Performers
Pierre Bernac (baritone), Francis Poulenc (piano) Documented

The Internet Archive item credits Pierre Bernac and Francis Poulenc and lists baritone and piano; the 1947 supplement says “with the composer at the piano”.

[1] [2]
Work version
The six songs for voice and piano (Le Dromadaire, La Chèvre du Thibet, La Sauterelle, Le Dauphin, L’Écrevisse, La Carpe); the edition is not stated. Documented

The dealer’s supplement lists the six titles and says the composer is at the piano. Johnson’s note gives the six poems as numbers 10, 4, 17, 19, 22 and 23 of Apollinaire’s collection. The printed edition used by the performers is not named.

[2] [4]
Recorded
Not stated Unknown

The record was listed as an import by April 1947 and appears in a numbered list of reviewed records in The Gramophone of September 1947, with a reference to the August issue, p. 34. The session date is not given in the sources consulted.

[1] [2] [3]
Place
Not stated Unknown

No source consulted names the studio.

[1]
Label
His Master’s Voice (HMV), 12-inch 78 rpm Documented

The supplement lists a 12-inch imported record, No. G-DB6299, with Montparnasse on the other side.

[1] [2]
Catalogue
DB 6299 Documented

The Internet Archive label data read “D.B.6299”; the list in The Gramophone reads “H.M.V. DB6299”.

[1] [2] [3]
Matrix, take, sides
2EA 10804-1 (Le Bestiaire); Montparnasse on the other side, 2EA 10807-1 Documented

From the item description of this side and of the separate transfer of the Montparnasse side. The take number of the matrix is as given by the transferring archive.

[1]
Transfer
George Blood, L.P., for the Great 78 Project (Internet Archive); disc from the Bowling Green collection Documented

The item description names the engineer’s firm and lists the collections georgeblood and 78rpm_bowling_green.

[1]
Transfer date
Not stated; the item was made public on 3 November 2023 Unknown

The public date of the item is an upload date, not the date of the transfer.

[1]
Processing
Four stylus sizes were tried; the preferred version was equalised with turnover 375 Hz and roll-off −12 dB, and copied under the friendlier file name. Documented

As stated in the item description. The published MP3 is the Internet Archive derivative of that file.

[1]
Composition rights
Poulenc died in 1963, so the music is in copyright in the EU under the life-plus-70 term, which runs to the end of 2033; national wartime extensions, which can lengthen the term for older works in France, were not assessed. The 1911 text is by Apollinaire, who died in 1918; rights in the poems are not assessed here. Documented

Rights in the composition are stated separately from rights in the recording. The United States status of the music is not established here.

[4]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial EU public domain: first published before 1963; on sale as an import by April 1947 and reviewed in The Gramophone in 1947. Documented

The United States status of a recording made in France in the 1940s is not established.

[2] [3]

Francis Poulenc, Le Bestiaire ou Cortège d’Orphée, FP 15. Pierre Bernac, baritone; Francis Poulenc, piano. HMV DB 6299, on sale as an import by April 1947. Transfer by George Blood, L.P., for the Great 78 Project; Internet Archive item 78_le-bestiaire_pierre-bernac-francis-poulenc-apollinaire-poulenc_gbia0525306a. Territorial EU basis (first published before 1963); US status not established. Rights statement

Internet Archive — LE BESTIAIRE (Pierre Bernac & Francis Poulenc): metadata and file inventory — metadata.description (matrix 2EA10804-1, catalogue D.B.6299, stylus and equalisation note), collections georgeblood and 78rpm_bowling_green; file LE BESTIAIRE - PIERRE BERNAC & FRANCIS POULENC.mp3 (4:44). Accessed 2026-10-19.
  2. The Gramophone Shop Supplement, April 1947 (Internet Archive scan) — Entry “POULENC: Montparnasse & Le Bestiaire … 12-inch imported record (2 sides), No. G-DB6299; price $2.62”. Accessed 2026-10-19.
  3. The Gramophone, September 1947, vol. 25 no. 292 (Internet Archive scan) — Numbered list of reviewed records: “H.M.V. DB6299. Le Bestiaire and Montparnasse (Poulenc), Bernac. Aug., p. 34”. Accessed 2026-10-19.
  4. Graham Johnson — note on Le bestiaire, ou Cortège d’Orphée, FP 15a, Hyperion CDA68021/4 — Apollinaire’s collection, the twelve settings, the reduction to six, the dedication to Durey, and the six poems chosen (numbers 10, 4, 17, 19, 22, 23). Accessed 2026-10-19.
  5. Apollinaire — Le Bestiaire, ou Cortège d’Orphée (1911), French Wikisource — Table of contents with page numbers; the pages for Le Dromadaire (16), La Chèvre du Thibet (10), La Sauterelle (24), Le Dauphin (27), L’Écrevisse (30) and La Carpe (31). Accessed 2026-10-19.
